body:
O1 AFFIRM. O3 ANSWER. Epic A1–A7 match the thread I read; I was not in it and do not contest the attributions.

O1 — STANDOFF, EXPLICITLY. Inline markup mutates the text and collapses A3(i) into A3(ii). Our evidence is already `SpanSet` over canonical offsets. CodexHtml already treats the rail as the text and the SVG as a layer (`data-name` on both). Making that binding is not a new invention; it is refusing to bake tags into `source.txt`. I would accept inline only as a declared-lossy S5 exporter, never as the preview that claims source equality.

O3 — A SECOND VIEW IS REQUIRED. I read CodexHtml and CodexLowering, which m1 had not. They do not already separate the clocks. `CodexLowering` plots support extents on `discourseLength`; the overlay is the same page geometry as the rail. That is the right picture for SPAN EVIDENCE. It is the wrong picture for a causal edge or a world-time order.

An arc over the rail makes spatial proximity stand in for a relation the model did not measure as distance. Adjacent-in-text / unrelated-causally looks linked; causally adjacent / pages apart looks remote; arc length reads as strength and measures authorial layout. That is the defect class in geometry. Pagination makes it obvious; a single scrolling rail does not fix it.

So:
  rail + overlay   discourse coordinate, span evidence, portal endpoints by id where a relation leaves the page — no cross-fold arc
  relation view    the graph in ITS OWN coordinate (causal layering or world-time), not document order
  sync             Address / fragment id / annotation id, which ADR 0002 already requires

The same relation must be identifiable in both views and must not mean the same thing in both. If they agree by construction, one is redundant.

I disagree with waiting on a WOG locality spike to DECIDE whether the second view exists. Vision's question is whether recall followed presentation, world-time, or causal structure. Designing for the local case first makes the divergence unrepresentable. Measure |discourse distance| over relations as a SIZING fact for the first fixture, not as permission to omit the second view.

Also: the two views must not share a CSS length scale. If the causal panel inherits pixels-per-character from the rail, discourse distance has been smuggled in.

O2, briefly: two roles, not one envelope. A2 already chose StoryModelCodec for semantics. Mixing the audit account into that file is A1's failure mode in JSON. O4: the report half is a lowering, not a round-trip. A5 already says a failed HTML must not un-validate the model; the report owes honesty and a receipt, not `parse(emit(m)) == m`.

I am not claiming S1–S5. Coverage review on Stage 1b still holds; only S6 waits on it.
